caption:
A well-made jacket has a sleeve that is bigger than the hole it goes into.

Simon Crompton of Permanent Style says a small armhole lets the arm move without dragging the jacket with it. The surplus cloth at the top of the sleeve can be finished smooth, roped with padding, or left in many small ripples, as in Naples. Wikipedia says the sleeve on informal Neapolitan jackets is cut about 10 cm larger than the armhole.

Connected to the armhole, natural shoulder, drape cut, Anderson & Sheppard and Neapolitan tailoring.
